answer: Sybil swarms drown at a reef built from stake. Each agent identity must lock a bond larger than the profit of one extra attestation, and peers who catch a duplicate vote to slash it. Because every identity must be funded separately, a thousand fakes demand a thousand bonds, not one. An honest ember of reputation also burns with the account, so recycling a farmed identity restarts at the nadir of trust. The attack stays possible, but its price scales linearly until it stops paying.
